title: High-ratio campaign: 6 of 15 sealed ARC-AGI-2 training tasks
goal: Solve at least six of the fifteen sealed ARC-AGI-2 training tasks in assets/gc-449/task_ids.txt -- a 40 percent solve-ratio demand that cannot be met by cherry-picking two easy tasks. The campaign needs a reusable toolkit: extract the transformation primitives that recur across solved tasks (symmetry completion, object counting, color mapping, gravity, occlusion repair, and whatever else the batch actually contains) into notes or code under runs/gc-449/primitives/, and show at least one later task solved measurably faster by reusing an earlier primitive. Grade after every two or three tasks, keep the solved count honest, and let the verdict history drive which rule families get the remaining budget.
resources: github repo: arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 pinned at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49 (task JSONs under data/training/ and data/evaluation/; each task file holds train pairs plus one or more test pairs)
assets/gc-449/task_ids.txt (sealed list of 15 task ids, one per line; all from the public training split; every id verified to exist in the pinned commit)
assets/gc-449/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: downloads the gold task files for the pinned commit, scores predictions cell-exactly, and prints {"solved": N} as its last JSON line)

output convention: runs/gc-449/predictions.json mapping task_id -> list with one entry per test input; each entry is a grid, a list of at most two attempt grids, or {"attempt_1": grid, "attempt_2": grid}
network: raw.githubusercontent.com must be reachable at grade time (the grader caches gold files under runs/gc-449/gold_cache/)
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-449/plan.md before the first prediction is written, naming per-task priorities, the attempt budget, and the exact verification command.

Every predicted task has a written transformation-rule hypothesis that was checked against every train pair before the test prediction; tasks where a hypothesis failed a train pair are logged by id with the revision that fixed it.
The grader was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.
The gold test outputs inside the pinned public repo are off-limits as inputs: predictions must be derived from the train pairs alone, and the run log must show that derivation per task.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-449/ledger.json records per-task attempts, spend, and outcome, including abandoned tasks and failed grader runs.
runs/gc-449/primitives/ holds the extracted transformation primitives, and the run log shows at least one later task solved by reusing an earlier primitive.
